src/ratings/notch.mjs named exports: RATING_SCALE = the 19 upper-case strings of C1 in order; notchChange(previous,current) = index(current)-index(previous), integer -18..18, positive downgrade, unchanged is +0 (never -0); notchCalculator(previous,current) -> exactly {notches, direction, wl}, notches = notchChange (C5), direction 'downgrade'|'upgrade'|'unchanged', wl 0 when notches<=1, 1 when 2, 2 when >=3. src/indicators/countryRating.mjs: countryRatingChangeWl(previous,current) -> 0 when notches<=0, 1 when 1, 2 when >=2, built on notchChange. Inputs are strings, trimmed and case-insensitive. WL above 2 is never produced.

items.answer: Every function throws RangeError when either argument, after trim and case-fold, is not one of the 19 ratings: empty/whitespace-only, null, undefined, non-strings (RangeError, not TypeError), out-of-scale ('D','SD','NR','CC','C','AAA+'), other notation ('Baa1'), internal spaces ('BBB +'), look-alike characters (Unicode minus). No fallback, no default WL, never swallowed.
Nothing exists to stay compatible with (repo holds only .gitkeep files). The exports become the public contract for later parts; names, signatures, signs and return shape are fixed by the Contract.

items.answer: Library: single-package modular monolith of pure ES modules, in src/ratings/notch.mjs and src/indicators/countryRating.mjs, tests under test/.

Two library modules in one package: ratings-notch (src/ratings/notch.mjs) and indicators-country-rating (src/indicators/countryRating.mjs, imports notchChange). Both owned by backend, reviewed by role reviewer. No service, BFF, app, worker or database.
Shared domain library of pure functions. No BFF, API or client layer in this slice (C8).
JavaScript ES modules (.mjs) on Node.js 18+, no npm dependencies, node:test with node:assert/strict. No APIs newer than Node 18 (no toSorted/toReversed/Object.groupBy).
No data stored; no persistence (C7), no I/O. RATING_SCALE is an in-code constant.
No external system; public-source fetch is out of scope, ratings arrive as arguments.
Synchronous, deterministic, idempotent pure functions; no queues or events.
No targets in the request; each call is a lookup in a fixed 19-entry list.
In-process library without dependencies; availability is that of the caller.

Only strict allow-list input validation applies (C1). Inputs are never used as a dynamic property key without validation, so '__proto__' or 'constructor' throw RangeError. No auth, authorisation or secrets (C7, C8).
Only rating codes are processed; not personal data. Nothing logged or retained.
Audit trail explicitly excluded from this slice.
No logging, metrics or tracing; modules do no I/O and C8 excludes printed output.
Only the business-confirmed WL thresholds and rating scale bind (C1, C2, C3, C6, REQ-03-12, REQ-03-13); implement exactly as stated.

node:test with node:assert/strict, *.test.mjs under test/, run by `node --test`. Devs write unit tests TDD; QA writes integration tests importing the public modules as a consumer: contract examples (C2, C6), every threshold boundary for both rule sets, sign convention (C5), normalisation, RangeError cases (C1). No coverage figure. Local Node 18+.
`node --test` must pass. No lint/typecheck/scan tooling (no dependencies may be added).
Nothing is deployed; consumed by ESM import. No flags or migrations. Rollback = revert the merge.
No separate documentation deliverable: the request asks for no README, changelog or runbook. The backend dev documents the exports with JSDoc inside the code card (PM decision, see events log).
